reviews.reasoning: Re-derived independently. Ps 27 is an identity psalm (web_mt_offset_map.json: rule "identity", web_verses 14 / mt_verses 14, mt_title_verses []), so oshb: cites owe no shift arithmetic, and verse_map_web Ps.27.0 carries is_title true with mt "inside Ps.27.1" — the row's "web:Ps.27.0 = oshb:Ps.27.1" is the owner-ruled title form and is arithmetically right. The mode claim holds against the bytes: imperatives in MT 27:1-6 = 0 in 6 verses, since v. 4 is perfect plus imperfect (שָׁאַ֣לְתִּי / אֲבַ֫קֵּ֥שׁ, oshb:Ps.27.4) and v. 6 is cohortative (וְאֶזְבְּחָ֣ה … אָשִׁ֥ירָה וַ֝אֲזַמְּרָ֗ה, oshb:Ps.27.6), while MT 27:7 opens with the imperative שְׁמַע (oshb:Ps.27.7, collate tier byte). The 6|7 seam is well warranted on both witnesses and I do not contest the span; the row's WEB quotes hold verbatim (check_web_quotes: 3 of 3 WEB quotations verbatim, 0 flags). The defect is confined to rejected_alternative, which grounds the whole-psalm rival in an evidence class the campaign excludes.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative grounds the one-composition rival in manuscript attestation ("share no independent manuscript evidence of separate origin"), cross-tradition material the campaign rules exclude as evidence in either direction, and states it as an unswept universal negative, unsupported by a cited witness.
challenges.evidence: TOOLKIT.md's cross-tradition rule and the review brief both place LXX/Vulgate/DSS/Qumran and versional material outside the admissible evidence set, in either direction. The row cites neither a witness nor a sweep for the negative. citation_sweep.py returns GREEN on this row because its cross-tradition guard keys on named traditions and does not catch generic "manuscript evidence" phrasing, so the violation is unguarded rather than absent. An admissible ground for the same rival sits in the bytes and is disclosed by neither row at this seam: occurrences of the root ישע in Ps 27 = 2 (unit: occurrences, skeleton tier), one on either side of the 6|7 seam — וְ֭יִשְׁעִי at oshb:Ps.27.1 (WEB “Yahweh is my light and my salvation.” web:Ps.27.1) returning as אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׁעִֽי at oshb:Ps.27.9 (WEB “God of my salvation.” web:Ps.27.9), both byte tier per collate.py --json. Under the cross-seam-cohesion rule a byte-true lexical return across the row's own seam argues continuity unless disclosed, so it is the warrant the rival actually needs; the cure is one edit installed on both rows at this seam.

reviews.reasoning: Verified and not contested. The opening quote שְׁמַע plus vocative, spliced as שְׁמַע יְהוָ֖ה, collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.27.7 (collate.py --json), and the gloss "hear, Yahweh" covers exactly the two quoted words, so quote and gloss are span-synced. Ps 27 is identity, so no dual-cite is owed. The v. 14 close is byte-real: קַוֵּ֗ה אֶל יְה֫וָ֥ה opens the verse and וְ֝קַוֵּ֗ה אֶל יְהוָֽה closes it (oshb:Ps.27.14), so the exhortation is genuinely doubled, and the WEB rendering the argument leans on is verbatim (check_web_quotes: 3 of 3 WEB quotations verbatim, plus 2 flags on curly-quoted Hebrew glosses carrying no inline web: ref in their field): “Wait for Yahweh. Be strong, and let your heart take courage. Yes, wait for Yahweh.” (web:Ps.27.14). pmarks_Ps.json places no selah, ketiv/qere, reversed nun or suspended letter in Ps 27, so no disclosure was owed. Two observations, neither rising to a defect. One: the doubling at v. 14 is verse-internal — it frames v. 14 itself, not vv. 7-14, since no form of קוה occurs at v. 7 — so the signal's "brackets the unit's own close" is accurate while the rationale's "brackets the unit" reads wider than the bytes support. Two: this span contains MT 27:13, whose opening word carries puncta extraordinaria on 3 of 4 consonants (U+05C4 upper dot and U+05C5 lower dot; the vav is undotted); that layer appears in no pmarks_Ps.json inventory, so no disclosure obligation exists and the row is not charged for it.

The span and the 5|6 seam verify. Ps 28 is identity (offset map rule "identity", 9/9 verses), so "web:Ps.28.0 = oshb:Ps.28.1" is the correct title form; verse_map_web Ps.28.0 is_title true, mt "inside Ps.28.1". The petition-verb description of vv. 1-3 holds at the bytes: אֶקְרָ֗א (oshb:Ps.28.1), the imperative שְׁמַ֤ע (oshb:Ps.28.2), the prohibitive אַל תִּמְשְׁכֵ֣נִי (oshb:Ps.28.3). The pivot the row hands to the next unit is real — MT 28:6 opens בָּר֥וּךְ יְהוָ֑ה, collate tier byte — and its WEB quotes hold verbatim (check_web_quotes: 6 of 6 WEB quotations verbatim, 0 flags). pmarks_Ps.json records no selah, ketiv/qere, reversed nun or suspended letter in Ps 28, so no disclosure was owed. The defect is a count-object blend in the v. 4 substrate signal.

challenges.claim: The signal quotes the pointed form תֶּן and asserts it "repeats twice in v. 4", but that byte string occurs once in MT 28:4 — the second imperative is תֵּ֣ן, a distinct form carrying tsere plus munach rather than segol.
challenges.evidence: Word-indexed splice of oshb:Ps.28.4 from verse_map_oshb.json: index 0 = תֶּן, index 7 = תֵּ֣ן, index 9 = הָשֵׁ֖ב. collate.py --json returns tier byte for all 3 against oshb:Ps.28.4, so the two spellings are independently quotation-grade and differ at byte tier. Occurrences of the quoted string in that verse = 1 (unit: occurrences of the pointed form); occurrences of the Qal imperative of נתן = 2 (unit: occurrences of the lemma). The row names a spelling and then counts a lemma, the blended count-object the semantic-class discipline forbids, and names no collate tier. The "third imperative" ordinal and הָשֵׁ֖ב itself are correct, and the seam is unaffected. The refrain row at 29:3-9 in this cluster shows the compliant form by naming both sweep mode and unit; this row does not. Cure: quote both forms, or name the object as the lemma and drop the pointed form from the count.

reviews.reasoning: The seam and the span verify; I contest two descriptive claims, not the boundary. MT 28:6 opens בָּר֥וּךְ יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ps.28.6, collate tier byte), a genuine petition-to-praise pivot, and the device_notes disclaimer is exactly right — the device inventory's book_boundary_doxologies hold 6 verse entries across 4 book seams (MT 41.14; 72.18-19 plus the 72.20 colophon, which the inventory marks baruch false; 89.53; 106.48), none of them in Ps 28, so the row's "four boundary doxologies" counts seams correctly and flagging this baruch as internal is well disclosed. The span closes the psalm at v. 9 (9/9 verses) and its WEB quotes hold verbatim (check_web_quotes: 3 of 3 WEB quotations verbatim, plus 3 flags on curly-quoted spans carrying no inline web: ref in their field). Both defects lie in the description of grammatical person and possession across vv. 6-9; the referential observation underneath them is itself sound, which is why neither rises above low.

challenges.claim: The signal states that the addressee widens from the psalmist (vv. 6-7) to “his anointed” (web:Ps.28.8) to “your people” (web:Ps.28.9), but second-person forms in MT 28:6-8 = 0 in 3 verses, so not one of those three is an addressee; the addressee in this span is Yahweh, and direct address starts at v. 9.
challenges.evidence: Second-person forms in MT 28:6-8 = 0 in 3 verses, spliced verse by verse from verse_map_oshb.json: 28:6 opens בָּר֥וּךְ יְהוָ֑ה כִּי שָׁ֝מַע … and 28:8 opens יְהוָ֥ה עֹֽז לָ֑מוֹ …, third-person report in 3 of 3 verses. Direct address begins at MT 28:9, whose imperatives are הוֹשִׁ֤יעָה, וּבָרֵ֥ךְ, וּֽרְעֵ֥ם וְ֝נַשְּׂאֵ֗ם — all 4 directed to Yahweh, with “your people” (web:Ps.28.9) as object rather than addressee. Verses in this span carrying direct address = 1 of 4 (unit: verses). What widens is referential scope, which the same sentence then correctly calls "a scope shift"; "addressee" is the error, and swapping the word repairs it without touching the warrant.

challenges.claim: The rationale's "the king's anointed" misassigns the third-person suffix on מְשִׁיח֣וֹ at MT 28:8, whose antecedent is Yahweh: the anointed one is himself the king, who does not possess an anointed.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.28.8 word index 5 = מְשִׁיח֣וֹ (collate tier byte), משיח with a 3ms suffix whose antecedent is the יְהוָ֥ה opening the same verse. WEB carries the same possessor: “Yahweh is their strength. He is a stronghold of salvation to his anointed.” (web:Ps.28.8). The row's own substrate signal quotes it correctly as “his anointed” (web:Ps.28.8), so rationale and signal disagree on the possessor inside one row.

reviews.reasoning: The 2|3 seam is right and I do not contest the span, but the row states its warrant in terms the bytes contradict twice, and since addressee distinctness is the boundary driver this row relies on — its 2 substrate signals both rest on it — the warrant as written does not carry the seam it reaches. Ps 29 is identity (offset map rule "identity", 11/11), verse_map_web Ps.29.0 is is_title true with mt "inside Ps.29.1", so "web:Ps.29.0 = oshb:Ps.29.1" is correct, and the device inventory records Ps 29's superscription as mt_title_verses "prefix_of_v1" with labels mizmor and le_david, consistent with that form. Its WEB quotes hold verbatim (check_web_quotes: 3 of 3 WEB quotations verbatim, plus 1 flag on a curly-quoted span carrying no inline web: ref in its field) and pmarks_Ps.json places no selah or ketiv/qere in Ps 29. The admissible and stronger statement of this seam is in the bytes: direct address exists in vv. 1-2 and ceases at v. 3.

challenges.claim: The signal quotes הָב֣וּ and claims it "recurs 3 times across these 2 verses (oshb:Ps.29.1 x2, oshb:Ps.29.2 x1)", but that byte form occurs once in MT 29:1, not twice — the second occurrence is הָב֥וּ — so the quoted form totals 2, and the dual-cited per-verse breakdown is false as written.
challenges.evidence: Word-indexed splice of oshb:Ps.29.1: index 2 = הָב֣וּ, index 6 = הָב֥וּ, which carries merkha where the quoted form carries munach; oshb:Ps.29.2 index 0 = הָב֣וּ. collate.py --json returns tier byte for הָב֣וּ against both oshb:Ps.29.1 and oshb:Ps.29.2, and tier byte for הָב֥וּ against oshb:Ps.29.1 — 2 quotation-grade spellings that differ at byte tier. Occurrences of the quoted string across vv. 1-2 = 2 (unit: occurrences of the pointed form); occurrences of the imperative of יהב = 3 (unit: occurrences of the lemma). Naming a spelling and counting a lemma is the blended count-object the semantic-class discipline forbids, and no collate tier is named; the dual-cited "x2" is what makes the defect machine-checkable rather than merely loose.

challenges.claim: The row's address analysis is wrong in both directions: the imperative is not "addressed to Yahweh" — its addressee is בְּנֵ֣י אֵלִ֑ים, with Yahweh the lamed-recipient — and "the storm's addressees from v. 3 forward" names a set that does not exist, since second-person forms across MT 29:3-9 = 0 in 7 verses.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.29.1 reads הָב֣וּ לַֽ֭יהוָה בְּנֵ֣י אֵלִ֑ים, where the vocative בְּנֵ֣י אֵלִ֑ים is the addressee and Yahweh the recipient — WEB renders it “Ascribe to Yahweh, you sons of the mighty, ascribe to Yahweh glory and strength.” (web:Ps.29.1); the same structure governs הִשְׁתַּחֲו֥וּ at oshb:Ps.29.2. Across MT 29:3-9, spliced verse by verse from verse_map_oshb.json, second-person forms = 0 in 7 verses and verses carrying direct address = 0 of 7 (unit: verses); the clauses are third-person report, e.g. ק֣וֹל יְ֭הוָה שֹׁבֵ֣ר (oshb:Ps.29.5) and וַיַּרְקִידֵ֥ם כְּמוֹ עֵ֑גֶל (oshb:Ps.29.6). Direct address therefore does not change addressee at v. 3, it stops — a sharper tier-1 warrant for the same seam than the one the row states, and one that passes the test that kills the original.

reviews.reasoning: The figures in this row re-derive correctly, and it is the one row here that names both its sweep mode and its unit rather than letting a pointed form stand as a count. I swept the refrain over Ps 29 independently from verse_map_oshb.json at skeleton tier: occurrences = 7, distributed vv. 3, 4 (x2), 5, 7, 8, 9 — 7 occurrences across 6 verses, matching the row's enumeration. It is verse-initial in 6 of 7 verses of the span (vv. 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9), absent from v. 6, which opens וַיַּרְקִידֵ֥ם כְּמוֹ עֵ֑גֶל … and continues the storm's effects rather than opening new content, and it is doubled in v. 4 — the signal's 3 claims check out. The quoted ק֥וֹל יְהוָ֗ה collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.29.3. Ps 29 is identity, so no dual-cite is owed. device_notes checks out twice over: the inventory's yhwh_elohim_per_psalm gives Ps 29 yhwh 18 / elohim 0, and my own per-verse token sweep returns 18 tokens in 11 verses; it is correctly marked as corroborating rather than driving. unit_type refrain_unit is in the controlled vocabulary and is earned by byte evidence even though Ps 29 sits outside the strategy's refrain roster. Confidence high is calibrated — this seam rests on a sevenfold verse-initial tier-1 device, not on texture. One observation, no defect: the sweep citation is span-scoped and would read more safely if it said so, because the same tool and needle return 7 verses / 8 token occurrences book-wide, the seventh verse being MT 106:25, and the digit 7 landing on two different objects invites a misreading that the row's enumeration forecloses.

The 9|10 seam holds and I do not contest the span. The opening substrate signal is exact: the refrain's closing occurrence is MT 29:9 and MT 29:10 opens יְ֭הוָה לַמַּבּ֣וּל without it (oshb:Ps.29.10), so the drop is byte-real, and the closing pair is properly bounded at the psalm's end (11/11 verses, identity numbering). Its WEB quotes hold verbatim (check_web_quotes: 2 of 2 WEB quotations verbatim, 0 flags). The second signal, however, is not discriminating, and with a single entry in boundary_evidence_refs it carries more weight than it can bear.

challenges.claim: The claim that "the doubled divine name pattern (Yahweh…Yahweh) recurs in both v. 10 and v. 11, unifying the closing pair", restated in device_notes as "the closing pair's own doubling pattern", is not discriminating: exactly 2 Yahweh tokens occur in 8 of Ps 29's 11 verses, so the pattern cannot mark the closing pair off from anything.
challenges.evidence: Per-verse Yahweh token sweep over Ps 29, spliced from verse_map_oshb.json at skeleton tier (unit: tokens, lamed-prefixed forms included): v1 2, v2 2, v3 2, v4 2, v5 2, v6 0, v7 1, v8 2, v9 1, v10 2, v11 2 — 18 tokens in 11 verses, agreeing with the device inventory's yhwh 18 for Ps 29. Verses carrying exactly 2 tokens = 8 of 11 (unit: verses), namely vv. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 10, 11. Six of those eight lie outside this row's span and four lie inside the refrain unit the row is distinguishing itself from, so the doubling is the psalm's dominant verse pattern rather than the closing pair's own. The row's discriminating evidence is the refrain drop it already states in its opening signal; this second signal should be withdrawn or replaced by the scope shift to לְעַמּ֣וֹ (oshb:Ps.29.11) that the rationale already argues (WEB “Yahweh will give strength to his people.” web:Ps.29.11).
